lines.text: AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE MANUAL
DMC-S1KDPDF-A-00-00-00-00A-040AD
Hydraulic power system
General description
1. General
The hydraulic power system supplies pressurized fluid to the flight control actuators, the landing gear retraction jacks,
the wheel brakes and the nose wheel steering unit. The system is arranged as two independent circuits, referred to
throughout this publication as the green circuit and the yellow circuit, so that the loss of one circuit does not remove
hydraulic power from any flight-critical function.
Each circuit has its own reservoir, engine-driven pump, filter assembly and accumulator. The circuits share no fluid
path in normal operation. A power transfer unit couples the two circuits mechanically, without transferring fluid, so
that a circuit whose pump has failed can still be pressurized from the opposite side.
WARNING
Do not disconnect any hydraulic line before the circuit has been depressurized and the accumulator has been discharged.
Residual pressure in an accumulator can be sufficient to cause injury.
Nominal system pressure is 3000 psi. The relief valve in each circuit opens at 3500 psi and reseats at 3200 psi.
Reservoir pressurization is taken from engine bleed air through a dedicated regulator; on the ground, with the engines
shut down, the reservoirs are pressurized by the hand pump on the ground service panel.
NOTE
All pressures quoted in this data module are gauge pressures measured at the system pressure transducer unless another
location is stated.
